who_can_apply: Age 16 or older. Can give at least 25 hours between mid-May and mid-September. Basic English.
how_to_apply: Apply when the page reopens. Then you do a 30 minute interview. Orientation is in early April. Training runs April to June.
notes: The day it reopens is not posted. Contact the Volunteer Coordinator through the page.
duration: Mid-May to mid-September, shifts of 2 to 5 hours
pay_detail: Unpaid. Every 25 hours earns ticket codes and access to dress rehearsals.

who_can_apply: Young people who are at least 12 and have not reached 19. Have your health card ready when you register.
how_to_apply: Choose Sea, Army or Air Cadets. Find a unit near you in the Corps and Squadron Directory. Register with the Online Registration Tool. Have your health card and your parents' contact details ready. Then unit staff contact you to check ID and welcome you.
notes: This is a Canada-wide program. The units in British Columbia come from the national directory. The British Columbia work rule is not verified for this card. A youth program, not a paid job.
duration: Not stated on the program pages
pay_detail: The program pages do not state a cost. The program page calls it a funded program. Ask the local unit about any fees.

who_can_apply: British Columbia youth ages 15 to 24 who want to work, go to school or start a training program and face barriers to doing so. You must be legally entitled to work in BC. You should not already be working, in school or in training, or be working less than 15 hours a week.
how_to_apply: Sign yourself up with the online Foundry Work & Education form linked on the Foundry services page. Or find a Foundry centre near you.
notes: Foundry also gives free and confidential mental health and wellness services for youth ages 12 to 24. WorkBC also lists this program. The British Columbia work rule is not verified for this card.
duration: Not stated on the program pages
pay_detail: Free. This is job and school support, not a paid job. Foundry says all its services are free and confidential.

who_can_apply: Students in high school. The pages give no grade or age rule. Check the Youth Train in Trades Guide and your school for rules.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school's career educator or work experience coordinator. Train in Trades uses a program guide and a registration form. Work in Trades signs you up as an apprentice with an employer sponsor. It uses a Youth Apprentice and Sponsor Registration Form.
notes: The British Columbia work permit rule for these jobs is not verified. Other ways to find an apprenticeship listed on the site include job boards, WorkBC centres and hiring fairs. Youth Explore the Trades lets you sample several trades. The SkilledTradesBC page, checked on 2026-10-10, is dated January 2024 and does not state a wage or say that Work in Trades is paid.
duration: From 1 high school course to a year-long program, depending on the program and trade
pay_detail: Youth Work in Trades training is paid, but no wage is stated. The youth programs page says tuition for these programs is covered. SkilledTradesBC and the Ministry fund technical training done in high school.

who_can_apply: Students who are active at a school or college. Your teacher, instructor or career coordinator must sign you up. The exact rules are in the provincial rules document.
how_to_apply: Talk to your teacher, instructor or career coordinator. They sign you up through the Skills Canada BC registration page. It needs a password. You get it from the organization or your regional coordinator.
notes: Students cannot sign themselves up. Regional registration goes through a teacher login. The provincial rule document at skillscanada.bc.ca/competitions/rules-and-regulations/ lists exact eligibility. The British Columbia work rule is not verified for this card.
duration: Regionals in February to March 2027, provincials on April 14, 2027
pay_detail: No fees are listed on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Highline Public Schools high school students at least 16 by August 17, 2026 who live, work or learn in Burien. Priority goes to those who live in Burien.
how_to_apply: Apply online. About 40 applicants get a 20 to 30 minute online interview. Info sessions were held in May and June 2026.
notes: You must be comfortable outdoors for up to 5 hours and walk 1 to 3 miles on uneven ground. Questions: education@mtsgreenway.org. The page states a $1,200 stipend for full attendance.
duration: 2 weeks, Mon to Fri, 9 AM to 2 PM (2026: Aug 17 to 28)
pay_detail: Stipend. The amount is not stated on this page. You also get a gear kit (pants, boots, shirt, hat, gloves, tools).

who_can_apply: Age 16 or older (18 for the Emergency triage role). Must give 3 hours a week for 8 months.
how_to_apply: Apply online. It takes about 30 minutes. If you are picked, you get an interview. You also need a police record check and references. Then you go to orientation and training.
notes: Call Volunteer Resources at 604-412-6130. The page was last updated on Jan 22, 2025.
duration: One 3-hour shift a week for at least 8 months
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Age minimums by course. Bronze Medallion is 13 or older. You must swim 400 m in under 12 minutes. Bronze Cross is 13 or older. First Aid is 14 or older. Lifeguard and instructor courses are 15 or older.
how_to_apply: Check the age and skills table. Then sign up for courses with the City (WebReg). You can also ask at a rec center with an indoor pool. Email questions to the address on the page.
notes: The page says extra certificates help but are not required to be a lifeguard with the City. This covers the instructor and fitness leader certificates. Pay and job age rules are not stated. The page says courses can earn high school credits.
duration: Several courses in a series
pay_detail: Course fees not stated on the program page. The page says lifeguard jobs have great pay and flexible hours but gives no rate.

who_can_apply: Age 14 or older. If you are under 18, a parent must say yes. You need good English, health coverage, 2 references and the right to volunteer in Canada. You must be able to walk the 10 acre site.
how_to_apply: Pick a job on the museum volunteer page. Then apply online.
notes: The page lists the intake months but not the year, so confirm the next date. The City of Burnaby volunteer page also lists Camps and playgrounds volunteering for youth 14 and older.
duration: At least 1 year and 35 hours of service per year
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Girls who are in grade 12 or will enter it in 2026 and live in British Columbia (2026 camp).
how_to_apply: Watch campignite.com for the next form. Email info@campignite.com. Do not email to ask how your form is going.
notes: Camp page is inconsistent: it says three days and also four days three nights. Confirm details on the next posting. Other Ignite camps run on Vancouver Island and in the Kootenays.
duration: Three full days, Aug 7 to 9, 2026 (the page also has a four-day, three-night description, so confirm)
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the program page. Run by a not-for-profit that aims to keep it affordable.

who_can_apply: You must be at least 14 years old and able to give at least one 3 or 4 hour shift each week.
how_to_apply: Check the page for when applications reopen. After you send the paperwork, you have an interview with volunteer services. Questions: 425-640-4341, Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
notes: Swedish's Issaquah and Mill Creek sites take only volunteers who are 18 or older. Providence Everett has its own junior program. It starts at age 16.
duration: At least one 3 to 4 hour shift a week
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer. It can count toward a school community service requirement.

who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must be low income. You must meet citizenship, residency or other approved status rules. You must meet background rules. You must be ready and motivated. The pages do not explain rules for applicants under 18.
how_to_apply: Go to enroll.jobcorps.gov. Click Apply Now. Make a MyJobCorps account. Upload the papers that show you are eligible. Then have an interview with an admissions representative. Phone for Curlew and Columbia Basin: 877-763-0580.
notes: Addresses: Cascades, 2060 Powerhouse Drive, Sedro-Woolley, WA 98284. Curlew, 3 Campus St, Curlew, WA 99118. Columbia Basin, 6739 24th Ave NE Bldg 2402, Moses Lake, WA 98837. Job Corps is a training program, not a job. Each center page shows only a few of its trades; use See More on the center page for the full list.
duration: Not stated on the program pages
pay_detail: Training is free. The national site lists free housing, meals, basic medical care and a living allowance. The allowance amount is not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Teens. The page does not state ages; ask the teen librarian at your branch. Each board sets its own meeting schedule.
how_to_apply: Contact your local librarian (Teen Services Librarian). Or go to an open Teen Advisory Board meeting listed on the page. If your branch has no board, ask about starting one.
notes: KCLS serves King County outside the city of Seattle (its branches include Maple Valley, Lake Forest Park, Newport Way and Federal Way). The Seattle Public Library volunteer page showed no current volunteer openings when read on 2026-10-09. Washington L&I says its child labor rules 'only apply to minor employees, not volunteers.'
duration: Ongoing; meeting schedules vary by branch
pay_detail: Unpaid. Members earn volunteer credit, and can ask for a reference letter after 10 hours of volunteering within 6 months.

who_can_apply: Park clean-up age 10 and up (10 to 14 with an adult). Mini-camp assistant age 13 and up. School field-trip assistant is 18 and up.
how_to_apply: The 2026 summer mini-camps are at capacity for volunteers. Fill in the online volunteer form on the page and choose the position.
notes: The page does not say whether applications are accepted on an ongoing basis. A police check is not stated on the program page.
duration: Mini-camp: at least one full camp. Clean-up: up to 1 hour a week.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteers get a free pin, a yearly certificate and a membership discount.

who_can_apply: Teens in grades 8 to 12. Volunteers who work with the public must pass a criminal background check.
how_to_apply: Fill in the teen volunteer form on the library page when it opens.
notes: Questions: 604-998-3450. The Dec 17 date comes from the Teens' community hub page. Exact roles are not listed on the page.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Age minimums by course. Bronze Medallion is 13. First Aid is 15. National Lifeguard is 15. Swim Instructor is 15. Lifesaving Instructor is 16. To apply for a job, you must be a citizen, a permanent resident or have a valid work permit.
how_to_apply: Sign up for courses online. After you are certified, apply on the NVRC job site. Email swim@nvrc.ca with questions.
notes: Courses need 100% attendance. Withdraw 8 or more days before the start for a full refund. The minimum age to be hired is not stated on the pages.
duration: Several courses
pay_detail: Course fees not stated on the program pages. Job pay not stated.

who_can_apply: Age 14 or older. Some roles need an older age or certificates (for example Aquatics needs age 15, Bronze Cross and Swim Instructor). Fitness volunteers must be 17 or over. Under 18 needs a parent signature.
how_to_apply: There are eight steps. Fill out the online form. Give two references. Sign the volunteer agreement. Get a police check at the RCMP where you live. Sign the photo release. Upload your forms. Go to orientation. Then email volunteer@nvrc.ca.
notes: Contact volunteer@nvrc.ca or 604-983-6345. The police check must be done where you live.
duration: Varies. Early years roles ask for 4 to 6 months.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Domestic students in North Vancouver School District, mainly grade 12. Seats are limited.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school Career Program teacher. If you missed the deadline, email jkinakin@sd44.ca.
notes: The page lists 16 programs.
duration: Not stated on the page
pay_detail: Tuition covered by the school board

who_can_apply: The page says its volunteers are over 16 years old. You need to be grown up, on time and good at talking with people.
how_to_apply: Fill in the North Shore form online. It takes 4 to 8 weeks. VCH runs a record check. Then you have an interview, reference checks and training.
notes: North Shore Volunteer Resources: (604) 984-5929, nsvolunteer@vch.ca. VCH's Vancouver program (VGH, UBC Hospital, G.F. Strong) does not state a minimum age on its pages, so ask vanvolunteer@vch.ca before applying there.
duration: 2 to 3 hours a week for at least 6 months
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer. Volunteers can get reference letters and recognition.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 19 during the program. You must be able to attend the whole season.
how_to_apply: Check the program page for the next application. Email dusty@goodgrub.org or call 360-753-5522.
notes: The farm is at 2016 Elliott Ave NW, Olympia. GRuB also runs other programs for teens and young adults, including GroundED for youth working on a GED.
duration: About 8 weeks, Tue and Thu 9 AM to 1 PM, Wed 11 AM to 5 PM (2026: July 7 to Aug 27)
pay_detail: Up to $1,000 educational stipend award, plus fresh farm food most weeks.

who_can_apply: Teens in grade 8 to 12. Members join the library volunteer team.
how_to_apply: Email teenblog@yourlibrary.ca to learn more. You can also look at the library volunteer page for other jobs.
notes: Full when read, so confirm first. Email teenblog@yourlibrary.ca.
duration: Meets the first Tuesday of each month
pay_detail: Unpaid. You earn service hours.

who_can_apply: Students now in grades 10 to 12. You must do an interview and a fitness test.
how_to_apply: Download the application when posted, or ask at your school career programs board or RCMP liaison officer. Then interview and fitness test.
notes: Exact August dates are listed as to be decided. Email careerprograms@sd38.bc.ca.
duration: One week, Monday to Saturday, in August 2027 (exact dates to be decided)
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the program page

who_can_apply: Richmond SD38 students. Must be a Canadian citizen or permanent resident. Grade 11 students apply to start in semester 2 of Grade 12.
how_to_apply: Get the form on the district page once it is posted. You can also get it at the school Career Programs board.
notes: Earns 16 high school credits and 12 KPU credits. Opening date not posted.
duration: Feb to June 2028, 4 courses
pay_detail: District pays tuition

who_can_apply: Students registered in a Richmond SD38 school. English 12 and Math 11 at 67% or higher, strong attendance.
how_to_apply: Get the application form from the district page or the school Career Programs board.
notes: The page lists no contact name or email. Get the application form from the district page or the school Career Programs board. The page says applications for 2027-28 are open and due the year before the program; no due date is printed.
duration: February to June, 4 courses
pay_detail: District pays tuition. Books, supplies and travel are the student's cost.

who_can_apply: Students at Richmond SD38 schools. Sixteen trades are offered. Some are welding, wood building, electrical work, cooking, car repair, plumbing and hair styling.
how_to_apply: Get the form from the district page. You can also ask your counsellor or career advisor. Or check your school Career Programs board.
notes: Email careerprograms@sd38.bc.ca for questions. The page gives no grade eligibility. The page's school-year wording conflicts: the headline says 2025-2026, the linked PDF says 2026-2027, and the body says 2027-2028. Confirm the year with the district before applying.
duration: One full program, taken in the 2027-28 school year for this intake
pay_detail: Unpaid. The school district pays tuition for the first level (the page says this often saves $2,500 to $5,000).

who_can_apply: Students ages 15 to 19 who have a job in a known trade. A skilled worker called a journeyperson must agree to sponsor you.
how_to_apply: Contact the district coordinator by the email or phone on the page.
notes: Contact Peter Thackwray, pthackwray@sd38.bc.ca, 604-668-6000 ext 1463. Courses are taken off the timetable. You need a trades employer first. Written for Richmond students.
duration: 120 paid work hours plus 3 short online assignments per course, up to 4 courses (16 credits)
pay_detail: Paid by the employer. Rate not stated. Finishing may earn a $1,000 scholarship from the Ministry of Education and Child Care.

who_can_apply: The Richmond page says its volunteers are over 16 years of age. VCH looks for people who are reliable, patient and mature and who will follow its rules.
how_to_apply: Fill in the Richmond form online. It takes 4 to 8 weeks. VCH runs a criminal record check. Then you have an interview, reference checks, orientation and training.
notes: Call Richmond Volunteer Services at 604-278-9711 ext. 384731, or email rhs.volunteerservices@vch.ca. Sites include Richmond Hospital, Minoru Residence, Richmond Lions Manor and Bridgeport. Use the 'Fill in an application' link on the Richmond page. VCH also links a fact sheet for Richmond applicants. It is a PDF, and it did not open on Oct 19, 2026.
duration: 2 to 3 hours a week for at least 6 months
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer. Volunteers can get reference letters, awards and events.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 15 to 20. 20 spots, first come first served.
how_to_apply: Sign up through City of Richmond program sign up. The course ID for 2026 is 00530586.
notes: Held at Minoru Centre for Active Living and Richmond City Hall. Next summer dates not posted when read.
duration: 3 days, 10am to 4:30pm
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: Youth 13 to 24. Anyone, including you, can refer you. You can drop in without a referral to check it out.
how_to_apply: Fill in the referral form and talk with a Youth Outreach Worker, or just drop in. Email medialab@richmond.ca or call 604-247-8303.
notes: It is at the Richmond Cultural Centre Annex, 7660 Minoru Gate. It works with Richmond Addiction Services Society. You get in by referral. It is not a job.
duration: Weekly drop-ins and seasonal programs
pay_detail: Free to join

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 18 with an IEP, a 504 plan or other proof of a disability. Tacoma Public Schools students and other students can join.
how_to_apply: Fill out the ANEW form linked on the Tacoma Public Schools summer credential page. Contact Stacy Kidd, who is listed on the page.
notes: The Tacoma Public Schools page says this is not an official Jobs 253 program. ANEW location is Lincoln High School per the page. The page lists Cohort 2 as July 13 to 16 but also says M to F, so confirm dates with ANEW. Work permit rule not stated.
duration: 40 hours of training. 2026 cohorts: July 6 to 10 and July 13 to 16, 7 a.m. to 3 p.m., at Lincoln High School
pay_detail: Paid training. $500 completion stipend.

who_can_apply: Students enrolled in grades 9 to 12 in a high school, Running Start, GED or homeschool program when they apply. Tides is the easiest level (any high school-aged person); Currents is the hands-on volunteer level.
how_to_apply: Attend a required online info session, then complete the application, then interview. Accepted teens do training before starting shifts. Questions: YOA@seattleaquarium.org.
notes: The page says its timeline is rough and may change. Washington L&I says its child labor rules 'only apply to minor employees, not volunteers.'
duration: One school year or one summer; at least 8 activities of about 3 to 5 hours each; can stay until the summer after senior year
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program. The page does not mention a cost.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 10 to 12. Each summer SAM works with one community group that serves young people, so spots go through that year's partner.
how_to_apply: The page does not explain how a student signs up. Email teenprograms@seattleartmuseum.org to ask about the next summer's partner.
notes: Past projects redid the South Park Community Center teen room and a school computer lab. If you are paid as an employee, ask whether you need Washington parent and school papers for a minor.
duration: Four weeks in August. Exact dates depend on the project and partner.
pay_detail: The page says it is a paid opportunity but does not give the amount.

who_can_apply: High school-aged youth who care about leadership, community and art. The page does not list other rules.
how_to_apply: Apply through the TAG page when the application opens in spring. The process includes a virtual interview.
notes: The page gives only a typical month (May), so watch the page in spring. Questions: teenprograms@seattleartmuseum.org. SAM's other internships are for college students and early-career adults, not high schoolers. If you take the stipend, ask whether you need Washington parent and school papers for a minor.
duration: Thursday evenings, October to May
pay_detail: Members receive community-service learning credits or a stipend for taking part. The page does not give the stipend amount.

who_can_apply: You must be 16 or older. Your application must name one or more volunteer roles. SAM cannot place everyone who applies.
how_to_apply: Read the list of roles, then use 'apply now' on the volunteer page and name the roles you want.
notes: SAM does not accept court-ordered volunteer hours. Library roles usually need library experience. Teens who want a deeper program can also look at SAM's Teen Arts Group.
duration: Most roles: at least 6 months, 2 shifts a month of 2 to 3.5 hours. Some roles ask for a year. Park Steward runs June to October.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer.

who_can_apply: Ages are not stated on the YouthForce page. Contact the program to ask.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply button for the TeamWork Internship or the Contact Us buttons on the YouthForce page. Call (206) 436-1843 if urgent.
notes: The page does not give ages, pay amounts, or an application window. Ask about age and school rules before applying. Work permit rule not stated.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Paid internships. Pay amount not stated.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12. Priority goes to teens with limited access to STEM role models or science resources.
how_to_apply: Apply online when a new session opens (see the Burke-ology page). Join the e-newsletter for dates.
notes: Not paid. The page lists no meeting dates for the session; the e-newsletter is the way to get them.
duration: Sessions run by topic (a spring 2026 session studied paleobotany); dates are posted on the Burke e-newsletter
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: Students in grades 7 to 8 who are 13 or older. Priority goes to teens who want to build confidence in STEM and those with few STEM role models or science resources.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the next session opens (the 2026 form was linked from the page). Join the Burke's Youth and Family Programs e-newsletter for dates.
notes: High schoolers can look at the Burke's Burke-ology program for grades 9 to 12. Burke volunteering is for ages 18 and up.
duration: Six Sundays, 2 to 5 p.m. (the 2026 session ran Oct 18 to Nov 22 at the Burke Museum)
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: People 16 and over for some positions and 18 and over for others. You must meet the minimum age when you apply.
how_to_apply: Apply online during an open period (you have one hour to finish), complete online training and forms within 2 weeks, do a 1-hour virtual group interview, then accept a placement. Onboarding includes a Washington State background check, an in-person health screening and a 90-minute orientation. Email VolunteerServices@seattlechildrens.org or call 206-987-4655.
notes: The youth service projects page (for ages under 16, such as donation drives or junior guilds) still carries a COVID-era notice, so it may be out of date. Nearly all shifts are weekdays starting between 9am and 2pm. Washington L&I says its child labor rules 'only apply to minor employees, not volunteers.'
duration: Most shifts are 3 hours on the same day and time every week; at least 6 months in a row (check each role)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteers get a badge and free on-site parking.

who_can_apply: Students in grade 10 or 11 who live close enough to travel to downtown Seattle. You need no research experience. You must have a Social Security Number or ITIN to take part.
how_to_apply: Apply online and send a letter of support. You must go to an orientation in person. In 2026 it was May 21, 4 to 5:30 p.m.
notes: Competitive: the 2026 lab has capacity for 24 students. The 2026 stipend is $2,000 to cover transportation and meals, and the IRS treats it as reportable income. Not a medical program and no patient contact. Work permit rule not stated.
duration: 4 weeks, weekdays 8:30 am to 3 pm (2026: July 13 to Aug 7)
pay_detail: Free. A stipend is paid to cover transportation and meals (amount not read).

who_can_apply: Students now in grades 10 to 12. Grades 10 and 11 go first. You must have taken at least one science course. You must live close enough to travel to downtown Seattle. You need a device with internet.
how_to_apply: Online application when the next cycle opens. Check the page.
notes: Hybrid (virtual and in person). Each research consultation also has a stipend, amount not stated. Breakfast and lunch are provided at the in-person training; students arrange their own transportation. Work permit rule not stated.
duration: Four 1.5-hour training sessions (the 2025 training day was a Saturday, Nov. 1, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.), then monthly 1-hour hybrid sessions and consultations through the year
pay_detail: $200 training stipend

who_can_apply: High school students who are 16 by the start date, live in the Seattle metro area (map on the page), and have valid ID and proof of US work eligibility. New-to-environment teens are encouraged.
how_to_apply: Online application at King County. No resume or cover letter. Answer the supplemental questions in detail. About 30 applicants get a 30 minute online interview.
notes: Washington requires a signed parent and school authorization form for every worker under 18 (L&I page). Only 12 interns in 2026. Interns meet in downtown Seattle and are encouraged to ride transit, which is free for youth.
duration: About 5 weeks, Monday to Friday, about 27 hours a week (2026: July 7 to Aug 7)
pay_detail: $22 an hour in 2026

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 22. You must complete the Cadet Program Physical Ability Test, meet attendance expectations and want to be a Seattle firefighter.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Fire Cadet application and email it with the required documents to SFD_Cadets@seattle.gov. See the selection process guidelines on the page.
notes: This is training, not a paid job. The city page also describes the department as encouraging women, people of color, immigrants and refugees to apply.
duration: Saturdays 8 a.m. to noon
pay_detail: Initial cost $95 plus $10 a month dues. Extra fees for special trips. Financial help is available. You buy your own uniform and safety shoes.

who_can_apply: High school students entering senior year who are 16 or older by the program start. You need strong science interest. You must live in Greater Seattle or nearby. Out-of-state and international students are not accepted. You must be free for all eight weeks and able to do a Zoom interview.
how_to_apply: Online application with short essays, email addresses for two references (they get a recommendation link after you submit), a PDF transcript and a PDF resume. Applicants must be able to attend a Zoom interview with the selection committee.
notes: Highly competitive and designed for students without much research experience. Fred Hutch does not provide or arrange housing, and interns arrange their own transportation. In Washington there is no permit the teen carries: the employer must hold a minor work permit endorsement, and a parent/guardian (and the school during the school year) signs a parent authorization form (Parent Authorization for Summer Work if hired during summer break only) before the minor starts.
duration: 8 weeks full time (2026: June 22 to Aug 14)
pay_detail: Paid internship; the amount is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Up to 18 high school students in the WANIC Skill Center service area. Chosen by lottery plus a meeting with a program leader. First-time participants get priority.
how_to_apply: Sign up on the WANIC summer course site during the application window. Then meet with a program leader and your family.
notes: Meet daily at the Riverview Learning Center in Carnation. Transport to field sites is provided. You must attend all 5 weeks. Questions: education@mtsgreenway.org. The page states a $1,800 stipend for full attendance and 1.0 CTE credit toward graduation.
duration: 5 weeks, Mon to Fri, 8:30 AM to 3:30 PM (2026: June 29 to Aug 4)
pay_detail: Stipend plus credit toward graduation. The amount is not stated on this page. A gear kit is provided.

who_can_apply: You must be 16 or older to help at the front desk. You must be 18 or older for patient units and clinics. If you are under 18, a parent must sign. You can only work Monday to Friday, 8 am to 5 pm.
how_to_apply: Apply online when it reopens and pick an in-person orientation date. Send proof of MMR, chickenpox and Tdap shots (and a flu shot October to March). Finish about three hours of online training, then pass a Washington State background check.
notes: Applications with missing shot records are denied, with no exemptions. It can take a few months to hear back. The volunteer office does not set up doctor shadowing. Questions: hmcvol@uw.edu.
duration: Four hours a week for six months in a row. No summer-only spots in the main program.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer.

who_can_apply: High school students in the Seattle area who care about modern art.
how_to_apply: The only call for applications found is from 2023-24, so check the Henry teen page or ask the museum if a new call is open. Submit the Call for Applications form when it is open.
notes: The teen page lists ages 14 to 18 but the application page found is old (2023). The page does not state cost; confirm cost and the current cycle before relying on it.
duration: Weekly meetings through the school year
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: High school students entering grades 10 to 12 in the school year after the summer. Only six spots. You do not need to be a history fan.
how_to_apply: The page says the 2026 deadline has passed. Check back in spring 2027 for information about next year's session (details on the History Lab page).
notes: Very small group (6 teens). Based at MOHAI with some field trips. Work permit rule not stated.
duration: 2 weeks, Monday to Friday 10 am to 4 pm (2026: July 27 to Aug 7)
pay_detail: $150 stipend for the work

who_can_apply: You must be at least 16 years old and pass a background check and a reference check.
how_to_apply: Fill in the general volunteer application (ages 16 and up) on the volunteer page. If your background and times fit, MOPOP sets up an interview. Questions: volunteers@mopop.org.
notes: MOPOP will verify service-learning hours for school. Its summer Youth Volunteer program for high schoolers 16 and 17 is paused; it last ran July 9 to Aug 20, 2025. Sound Off!, its showcase for musicians 21 and under, is paused in 2027.
duration: At least 6 months, one shift every other week (9:45 a.m. to 1 p.m. or 1 to 4 p.m.)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer. Volunteers get free admission with a guest, special events, discounts and parking help.

who_can_apply: Students ages 15 to 18. You may serve for up to three years.
how_to_apply: Watch the YAB page for the next application. Questions go to YAB@MOPOP.org.
notes: The page does not say when the next call opens or whether members are paid. Email YAB@MOPOP.org to ask.
duration: Meets every other week during the school year; up to three years
pay_detail: The page does not say if members are paid or if there is a cost.

who_can_apply: Teens and camp grads ages 13 to 17. All-Time Belayer: ages 13 to 17. Junior Counselor: ages 15 to 17. You do not need camp or climbing experience; training is given.
how_to_apply: Apply on the CIT page when applications open in March 2027. Questions: summercamp@mountaineers.org.
notes: A nonprofit summer camp, not Seattle Parks. Pick the weeks that fit your schedule. Unpaid volunteer role; Washington L&I says its minor work rules apply to employees, not volunteers.
duration: All-Time Belayer: 9 am to noon, at least 6 days. Junior Counselor: 9 am to 4 pm, at least 2 weeks.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer. Junior Counselors can join a Camp Alumni Adventure trip at a highly discounted rate.

who_can_apply: The page says anyone age 16 and above can volunteer. Youth use the Youth Volunteer Application. One reference is required (the Youth Reference Form). Not all roles are open to youth.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Youth (16-17) Volunteer form. Attach the Youth Reference Form. The Volunteer Office reviews it and may set up an interview. New volunteers go to an orientation.
notes: Exact museum address is not on the page. The page does not state an upper age limit of 17; max_age is kept at 17 only because the card needs an integer, so confirm with the Volunteer Office (volunteers@museumofflight.org). Not a paid job.
duration: The museum asks for 8 hours a month; hours vary by role
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Mentorship is for ages 13 to 21. The paid internship is for ages 15.5 to 21 and requires finishing the mentorship first. An E-13 form is required under 18.
how_to_apply: Apply online for the mentor program. Links are on the page. Go to all four Saturdays. Then apply and interview for the summer internship. You must apply again each year.
notes: Food and supplies are provided. Mentorship location rotates around Seattle (North, Central, Southeast, Southwest). Interns can return for up to 3 years. Work permit rule not stated on the page.
duration: Mentorship: 4 Saturdays (28 hours), offered 5 times a year. Internship: 8 summer weeks, 20 hours a week.
pay_detail: Mentorship: $300 stipend if you attend all 4 Saturdays. Internship: Seattle minimum wage, listed as $21.30 per hour in 2026.

who_can_apply: Seattle Parks summer jobs are open to ages 16 and up (18 and up for some positions). Lifeguards need a current American Red Cross Lifeguarding, First Aid and CPR/AED certification. The Red Cross course requires you to be at least 15 on or before the last class. You must also pass a swim test.
how_to_apply: Get Red Cross certified. Then apply on GovernmentJobs.com when a listing is active, or email an Aquatic Application (or resume and cover letter) to parksaquatics@seattle.gov, or give it to the Aquatic Center Coordinator at any Seattle indoor pool. Hired lifeguards pass a background check, a physical and the NW Lifeguard Test. Call 206-684-4078.
notes: Red Cross certifications last 2 years. The cost of the Red Cross course is not stated on the Parks pages. Seattle Parks is a municipal employer; Washington L&I says state and municipal governments are not subject to Washington's child labor rules (federal rules still apply).
duration: Summer-only at beaches and outdoor pools, or year-round at indoor pools
pay_detail: Listed on the Parks summer jobs page as 'starts at $26.92' (the unit is not stated on the page).

who_can_apply: Jobs are open to ages 16 and up. Some jobs need you to be 18 (for example the disability programs). Some need a WA driver license or certifications. Read each job posting.
how_to_apply: Apply to each job on the City of Seattle jobs site through the Open Temp Jobs link. Many recreation programs hire through the nonprofit Associated Recreation Council instead.
notes: Washington requires a signed parent and school authorization form for every worker under 18 (L&I page). See the separate Seattle Parks lifeguard and aquatics training card for guard training.
duration: Wading pools run mid June to Labor Day. Boat ramp jobs run May to September.
pay_detail: Starting pay in the 2026 postings: $26.92 an hour (wading pool attendant, lifeguard), $33.47 (aquatics customer service), $34.08 (boat ramp ranger)

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 18 and in grades 6 to 12. You must first finish at least one cohort of the Youth Leadership Program (40 hours in a quarter).
how_to_apply: Finish the Youth Leadership Program first. Then apply when the window opens. You need a Participant E-13 form for internships. Contact the Late Night and Youth Leadership Coordinator listed on the page.
notes: Paid City of Seattle intermittent employee job. Sites include Bitter Lake, Garfield, Meadowbrook, Rainier Beach, Southwest and Van Asselt. Spaces are limited. The page does not mention a work permit.
duration: Two 6-month cohorts a year: January to June and June to December
pay_detail: City of Seattle minimum wage, listed as $21.30 per hour in 2026.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 9 to 18, aimed at youth of color. Auditions are held each spring.
how_to_apply: Audition in the spring. Contact the director listed on the page for sign-up details.
notes: Breakfast and lunch are provided. The page says costs are paid by ages 9 to 15 and stipends are paid at the end. Stipend for ages 9 to 12 is $300 per the page. 2026 auditions were April 17 and 18. Work permit rule not stated.
duration: 2026: rehearsals June 29 to Aug 27, shows Aug 28 to 30
pay_detail: Cost $350 for ages 13 to 15 ($400 for ages 9 to 12) but participants get a stipend: $599 for ages 13 to 15. Ages 16 to 18 are paid minimum wage ($21.30 per hour in 2026) every 2 weeks.

who_can_apply: Pre-Employment Training is for ages 13 to 18, and you can take it once every 2 years. It is the prerequisite for Parks paid internships (Teen Late Night, Summer, Community Learning Centers), which are for ages 15 to 21.
how_to_apply: Email PKS_Teen_Employment@seattle.gov (phone 206-684-4575) for details and to apply. The page also lists career readiness workshops (resumes, mock interviews, food handler permit help) at Teen Life Centers and community centers.
notes: Youth may do one paid internship at a time. Seattle Parks is a municipal employer; Washington L&I says state and municipal governments are not subject to Washington's child labor rules (federal rules still apply). The page also mentions free college tours for Seattle Public Schools students in grades 9 to 12.
duration: 7 weeks, 14 hours total, offered each Fall, Winter and Spring quarter
pay_detail: After finishing the training you may earn a $300 stipend or Service Learning credit toward high school graduation. Internship pay is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 21, full-time students with a 2.5 GPA or higher, no felony or serious misdemeanor, and able to pass a background check and oral interview. Under 18 needs a parent signature.
how_to_apply: Email Officer Tre Smith (tre.smith@seattle.gov) to attend a meeting. Attend 2 to 4 monthly meetings in a row, then get the application, then a background check and an oral board with current Explorers.
notes: Program is taught in English. Contact name is as listed on the page and may change.
duration: At least 2 meetings and 1 community event a month
pay_detail: Free to join. Hours count as service learning for high school.

who_can_apply: BIPOC girls and gender expansive youth ages 16 to 19 who live or go to school in or near Seattle and King County.
how_to_apply: Applications closed. Questions: aaron@powerfulvoices.org.
notes: Powerful Voices also lists other paid teen internships on its For Young People page (Activistas for ages 14 to 19, Artivism, DYVAS). Those pages do not post pay or dates, so they are not listed separately.
duration: About 3 months (2026: June 23 to Sept 22), about 5 to 7 hours a week, hybrid
pay_detail: $1,712 stipend, paid monthly

who_can_apply: BIPOC girls and gender expansive youth ages 13 to 19 (BIPOC adults 20 and up can also be fellows). Hybrid, Seattle area and online.
how_to_apply: Applications closed. Questions: healingjustice@powerfulvoices.org.
notes: Ask Powerful Voices whether the stipend counts as a job under Washington youth work rules.
duration: May to December 2026, 2 to 3 hours a week (more around events)
pay_detail: $20 an hour, up to $2,000 total

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 16. Grade rules are not listed. You need two recommendations, an interview, a health screening and orientation.
how_to_apply: Online application (Volgistics link on the page), two recommendations on the provided forms or in your own letters, then an interview with Volunteer Services.
notes: Volunteers who turn 18 and keep going must complete a national background check. Ask Volunteer Services about openings and the health screening.
duration: 48 hours, usually over about 3 months

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors from 22 partner high schools in Highline, Federal Way, Tukwila and Tahoma. Students from other districts need an Inter-District Agreement from their home district. You need to be on track to graduate. No minimum GPA.
how_to_apply: Apply in the online portal during the open window, then a lottery is used if there are more applicants than seats. Talk to your school counselor. Admissions: 206-631-7322.
notes: Consortium districts provide buses. Others provide their own ride. The Aeronautical Science program meets after school at The Museum of Flight.
duration: 1 or 2 years, half of each school day
pay_detail: Tuition-free. Earns 3.0 high school credits for a full year, with college credit options.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 18. Grades: entering 9th grade (fall 2026) through high school seniors. Selected teens must give a copy of a Social Security card and complete a W-9.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form linked on the SafeFutures internship page. If you are picked, you have 2 business days to say yes.
notes: Very competitive: the page accepts 20 applicants. The page URL says 2023 but the content is the 2026 program. The 2026 page states no stipend amount. Work permit rule not stated.
duration: 6 weeks, July 2 to Aug 14 in 2026, Monday to Thursday, 12 pm to 6 pm
pay_detail: Stipend paid after successful completion. 2026 page does not state the amount (older SafeFutures pages said $1,000).

who_can_apply: Crew members ages 14 to 18, currently in high school or recent high school graduates. Crew Leaders must be 21 or older.
how_to_apply: The page links to SCA's job listings. Call the SCA Seattle Office at (206) 693-3147.
notes: The page says "Check back next spring for our 2026 summer positions!", so the text may be out of date. Call (206) 693-3147 to ask when the next season is posted.
duration: July to August, about 35 hours a week
pay_detail: Paid. The wage is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18 who live or study in Seattle. No transportation experience needed. Only 15 spots.
how_to_apply: Online application, about 15 to 30 minutes. Selected teens under 18 need a parental consent form and a photo release form.
notes: Held at the Seattle Municipal Tower, 700 5th Ave. Youth 18 and under ride transit free. The page lists the 2026 application window as opening May 26 and closing June 16.
duration: About 4 weeks, Tuesdays and Thursdays 10 AM to 3 PM (2026: Aug 4 to 27)
pay_detail: $600 stipend at the end (you fill out a tax form)

who_can_apply: Teens who are 15 or older by May 19, 2027, not older than 19 during the program, enrolled in high school, with a Washington address and proof of US work eligibility.
how_to_apply: Create an account on Submittable, answer short questions, and get two letters of recommendation. Top applicants get a virtual interview.
notes: Washington requires a signed parent and school authorization form for every worker under 18 (L&I page). Competitive and interviews are not guaranteed. TIPS pays you, not the nonprofit. Free ORCA transit cards for youth up to 18 are mentioned on the page.
duration: 6 to 8 weeks, about 20 to 30 hours a week, plus 3 required training events
pay_detail: Seattle's minimum wage (projected $21.81 an hour in 2027), up to 160 hours, so up to about $3,490 before taxes

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 19.
how_to_apply: Check the TeenTix Program Applications page to see the current round. The page is teentix.org/programs/apply.
notes: The page says there is no cost to participate and all New Guardians receive monthly stipends (amount not stated). The program page's only year reference is 2025-26, and the TeenTix applications page says 2026/27 applications are closed, with the next round opening in Spring 2027. Confirm with TeenTix that New Guard runs in the next cycle. Work permit rule not stated.
duration: School-year cohort (dates not stated)
pay_detail: Free to join. Monthly stipend, amount not stated.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 19, from grade 8 through early college. About 30 to 40 teens join each year. You must review at least one event during the school year.
how_to_apply: Check the TeenTix Program Applications page to see the current round. The page is teentix.org/programs/apply.
notes: The Newsroom runs from September to June on the school year schedule. It is good for building a writing portfolio. Ask TeenTix how much writers are paid.
duration: September to June
pay_detail: The page says writers are paid for their writing. The amount is not stated. You also get free press tickets to the events you review.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 18. Crew members must be able to do heavy lifting and work in rain or shine.
how_to_apply: The page does not list the steps to apply. Contact Suez Gebretsadik at (206) 633-0451 ext. 900 or suezgebretsadik@tilthalliance.org.
notes: Pay, dates and how to apply were not stated on the page. Confirm with the contact before you plan around it. These are temporary seasonal positions.
duration: Spring, summer and fall positions
pay_detail: Not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Washington state residents enrolled in a Washington high school in 10th or 11th grade. No coding experience needed. The program aims to include economically disadvantaged and future first-generation college students; the home page says it is open to all rising juniors and seniors at Washington state high schools.
how_to_apply: Apply online by the deadline (every application submitted on time is reviewed equally). Questions: cic@cs.washington.edu.
notes: Students must be able to get to the UW campus on their own. Absences are limited: after four absences students are dismissed. The stipend is described as a stipend, not a wage. Paid work for people under 18 in Washington needs a parent and school authorization form (the employer holds the Minor Work Permit). See permit.html?state=wa for the exact permit and steps.
duration: 4 weeks, Monday to Thursday, about 9am to 3pm (2026: July 6 to 30)
pay_detail: Free. Every mentee gets a $1,200 stipend; lunch and materials are provided. No housing, and bus passes are not provided.

who_can_apply: Any Washington state high school sophomore or junior in the 2025-2026 school year can apply. You need no engineering experience. You get yourself to and from the UW Seattle campus.
how_to_apply: Apply online when it opens in March 2027.
notes: Free of cost to participants. The page is an introductory program for students curious about engineering. Work permit rule not stated.
duration: 1 week, Monday to Friday, 10 am to 4 pm (2026: July 20 to 24)
pay_detail: Free

who_can_apply: High school students (page lists rising 10th, 11th and 12th graders and graduating seniors; no age range stated). No business experience required.
how_to_apply: Apply through partner Summer Springboard's online portal (Apply now link on the page). Program questions go to the program contact listed on the page.
notes: Expensive paid pre-college program from a real university. The page says students can attend both experiences during a single extended stay, but it does not name a one-week Business Startup Bootcamp.
duration: 2 weeks (2026 session: July 5 to 17)
pay_detail: Commuter tuition $4,498 (lunch, a course, excursions, 9am to 5pm Monday to Friday). Residential adds $3,000. Commuters can join weekend excursions for $125 per day. Financial aid is not mentioned on the page.

who_can_apply: Washington state high school sophomores and juniors interested in nursing. You must be 16 before the first day of camp. The page says there are no exceptions.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the 2027 application opens. For a waitlist spot or questions, use the inquiry form or email uwnursecamp@uw.edu.
notes: The camp provides breakfast, lunch and snacks each day. The 2027 camp dates are not posted yet. Join the email list on the page for updates.
duration: 1 week, day camp (2026: July 20 to 24)
pay_detail: Free to attend. You cover your own transportation, meals and any overnight housing.

who_can_apply: U.S. high school students who have finished eighth grade or equivalent by June 30 of the summer. If under 18 on the first day, you and a parent must sign an Under 18 form.
how_to_apply: Apply online with the Summer Sessions form. Pay the $80 fee. Send the Under 18 form signed by you and a parent. Then sign up for courses once sign up opens.
notes: Costs real money and registration is first come, first served. Not a job or internship.
duration: Summer quarter (2026 started June 22)
pay_detail: $80 nonrefundable application fee plus UW Summer Sessions tuition (amount not read; see the UW tuition page).

who_can_apply: Community high school students. The page does not give an age range.
how_to_apply: Check the UW Medicine volunteering page in March 2027 for the application. For the waitlist, email uwmcvol@uw.edu.
notes: All UW Medicine volunteers must show required shots and pass a background check. The program does not offer job shadowing or internships. The adult program needs age 18 and a high school diploma, so the summer program is the teen route.
duration: Summer only (the page does not give the number of weeks)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer.

who_can_apply: Students in a public high school in Bellevue, Issaquah, Lake Washington, Mercer Island, Northshore, Riverview or Snoqualmie Valley. Private and homeschool students register with their local public high school. Outside students may join on a space-available basis with permission from their home district.
how_to_apply: Apply online through a WANIC parent account. Some in-district skill center classes use your school counselor instead. Questions: wanic@lwsd.org or 425-739-8400.
notes: Applications before March 31 get priority and are not first come, first served. Summer semester has no out-of-consortium students.
duration: Full school year (also a summer semester)
pay_detail: Tuition-free. You provide your own transportation.

who_can_apply: Anyone ages 13 to 19. All art levels welcome. Capacity is 15 students, first come, first served.
how_to_apply: Registration is first come, first served. Email youthcan@wingluke.org to ask about info sessions.
notes: Only 15 spots.
duration: After school, Wednesdays 4 to 6 p.m. The page gives no date for the group show.
pay_detail: Free. Students get a museum membership.

who_can_apply: High school students entering grades 10 to 12. No prior experience required. The teen page does not state a minimum age; 15 teen volunteers were taken in 2026.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application by the deadline. Email teenambassadors@zoo.org for help. Sign up for recruitment updates at zoo.org/volunteer.
notes: The zoo's general volunteer program has its own rules (at least 16, one-year commitment, applications opening January 2027); those do not appear on the teen page. Applicants who identify with autism or ADHD can get application and interview support from Canopy Neurodiversity Foundation. Paid work for people under 18 in Washington needs a parent and school authorization form (the employer holds the Minor Work Permit). See permit.html?state=wa for the exact permit and steps.
duration: June to September: orientation day, at least 7 of 10 Wednesday meetings (3:30 to 6:30 pm), 20 volunteer hours between June 29 and Sept 6 (2026 dates)
pay_detail: Active teen volunteers receive a $300 summer stipend to help with transportation, lunches and shoes. No participation fee is listed.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 6 to 12. Clubs are school based. A map on the page shows partner schools, or you can ask to start a new club.
how_to_apply: Check the school map and join your school club, or email yesc@seattleymca.org to start one or join events. Teens can also volunteer as event support.
notes: The page says almost 1,500 young leaders took part in 2023-24. It does not give event dates for this year.
duration: School year clubs; meetings last 30 minutes to 2 hours
pay_detail: No cost stated.

who_can_apply: Must be at least 16 years old and have First Aid and CPR certification (training is available). Overnight camp and BOLD & GOLD jobs need you to be 18.
how_to_apply: Apply for a Summer Day Camp job on the YMCA of Greater Seattle careers page. Questions: recruiting@seattleymca.org.
notes: Washington requires a signed parent and school authorization form for every worker under 18 (L&I page). The page also lists lifeguard and swim instructor jobs, which need to be at least 16 at branches or 18 for overnight camp. Y childcare discount is mentioned.
duration: Season runs June 20 to Aug 26 (start dates vary by location). Shifts are 8 hours, Monday to Friday, between 6:45 am and 6:15 pm.
pay_detail: Starts at $21.30 an hour

who_can_apply: Ages 17 to 24. Other eligibility rules are not listed on the page.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Today button on the page, which links to a YMCA job posting. You can also contact Ann Beasley at abeasley@seattleymca.org.
notes: Only 17 and 18 year olds are teens here. Washington requires a signed parent and school authorization form for every worker under 18 (L&I page). Confirm the pay and start date before planning around it.
duration: 10 weeks
pay_detail: $20.97 an hour for up to 135 hours over 9 weeks. The first week is unpaid.

who_can_apply: Any student in grades 8 to 12. No experience needed. Delegations meet at YMCA branches in Bellevue, Seattle, Northshore, Sammamish, Snoqualmie Valley and nearby.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form on the page and the Y connects you to the closest delegation. Email ygseattleyag@seattleymca.org with questions.
notes: The page also describes Mock Trial for grades 6 to 12, but no branch-based Mock Trial teams are offered in 2026-27.
duration: School year, with a statewide conference May 5 to 8, 2027
pay_detail: 2026-27: delegation fee $175 for Y members or $225 for others, plus conference fee $500. Financial help and payment plans are available.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 19 who live in Seattle or go to school in Seattle. Two-year term. Parent or guardian consent is needed if under 18.
how_to_apply: Email SeattleYouthCommission@seattle.gov to hear when applications reopen. Then apply. If you are under 18, add the parent consent form.
notes: Not a paid job. Good for civic and government interest. The page does not list a deadline.
duration: Two-year term; monthly hybrid meetings on the 4th Saturday of each month, 9 to 11 am, at City Hall
pay_detail: Unpaid. No fees. Can count toward Seattle Public Schools service hours.

who_can_apply: Age 16 to 24 at the start of the program (you can apply at 15 if you will be 16 by the start date). You must live in Seattle or attend Seattle Public Schools or Seattle Colleges, and household income must be at or below 80% of Area Median Income (for example $81,700 for 1 person, $116,650 for 4).
how_to_apply: Create an account and complete the online application at youthconnect.powerappsportals.us (the page links a help guide). The 250 internship spots are chosen by lottery. Pathways requires finishing SYEP Foundations or passing the Assessment of Skill.
notes: Proof of authorization to work in the U.S. is required for the internship, and an SSN or ITIN is needed to receive stipends and take part. The SYEP page does not mention work permits. Placements include City departments, which Washington L&I says are exempt from state child labor rules ('Public entities, including state and municipal governments, are not subject to Washington's child labor rules'; federal rules still apply), and private businesses and nonprofits, which are not exempt, so ask your placement about the parent/school authorization form. Questions: SYEP@seattle.gov or 206-386-1375.
duration: Internship about 6 weeks (July 6 to Aug 18, 2026). Foundations: October 2026 to March 2027 (tentative), 2-hour weekly sessions.
pay_detail: Internship: at least Seattle's minimum wage, listed as $21.30 per hour. Learn & Earn Foundations: $325 stipend at the end of each module. Pathways: monthly stipend, amount not stated.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 15 to 19 who identify as Black, Indigenous or a person of color, are in grades 10 to 12, and can attend every Tuesday and Thursday 4:30 to 7 PM for 17 weeks. Priority goes to teens without arts classes at school.
how_to_apply: Apply on the page. About 25 applicants are chosen to interview for 10 spots.
notes: Only 10 spots. Graduates can later be hired for Youth in Focus photo jobs. Exact dates are not set on the page.
duration: 17 weeks, about 5 hours a week in person plus 1 to 2 hours of homework
pay_detail: $1,400 stipend

who_can_apply: Teens who take part in Youth in Focus programs (ages 13 to 19) and have finished at least one of its free after-school photography classes.
how_to_apply: Finish at least one free after-school class (register on the Class Registration page). Staff pick a student for each event and send the details.
notes: Classes are free or pay what you can, and equipment, snacks and bus passes are provided. The page does not say whether the stipend is treated as a job for work-permit purposes, so ask.
duration: Event by event; students rotate
pay_detail: Stipend check mailed after each event. Amount not stated.

who_can_apply: Age 14 or older. You must have the right to volunteer in Canada.
how_to_apply: Fill in a form on MyImpactPage. Go to an interview. Send 2 references. Get a Police Information Check. It can take up to 6 weeks.
notes: Contact volunteer@surrey.ca or 604-598-5863. The page says interview slots are available to sign up for, but shows no dates. Intake status is unclear, so confirm first.
duration: At least 30 volunteer hours across the year
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 18 who live in Surrey.
how_to_apply: Wait for spring 2027 applications on the City of Surrey page. Email the youth team with questions.
notes: Meets Wednesdays 4:30 to 6:00pm at City Hall on the groups page. The council page says every other week. Spring 2027 date is the city's statement, exact day not posted.
duration: A school-year term, meetings every other week
pay_detail: Unpaid. You earn volunteer hours.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18. New volunteers send 2 references and go to a training session.
how_to_apply: Apply on the City of Surrey My Impact page (an account is needed). Send 2 references. Attend training before the program starts.
notes: You must attend all 6 sessions. Branches: City Centre, Clayton, Cloverdale, Fleetwood, Guildford, Newton, Ocean Park, Semiahmoo, Strawberry Hill. Spring dates not posted when read.
duration: 6 weekly sessions, 60 minutes each, twice a year (spring and fall)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Counts toward volunteer hours.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 18. New volunteers need two references. If you have not volunteered with the City of Surrey, the Teen Library Council or Reading Buddies in the past 12 months, you need a Police Information Check. Hand it in by July 31.
how_to_apply: Apply on the City of Surrey My Impact page (an account is needed). Send 2 references. Go to an orientation before the first meeting.
notes: Meets once a month from September to June at six branches: City Centre, Clayton-Cloverdale, Fleetwood, Guildford, Newton-Strawberry Hill and Semiahmoo-Ocean Park. If you miss three meetings in a row, you may lose your spot. British Columbia work paper rules were not checked. This is unpaid.
duration: Monthly meetings, September to June
pay_detail: Unpaid. You earn volunteer hours.

who_can_apply: Age 16 or older depending on the program. Parent or guardian consent is needed under 18. ICU, NICU and Palliative Care need age 20+.
how_to_apply: Apply online. If you qualify, you get an interview. Then you need a police record check and two references. You also do online orientation and training.
notes: Page last updated Aug 2, 2024. The STIR research program on the same page is for undergraduates, not high school.
duration: One shift a week on the same day for at least 6 months
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 18 who live, learn, work or volunteer in Surrey. You lead or take part in the project.
how_to_apply: Fill out the YEP Project Application Form.
notes: Funding requests are reviewed one by one.
duration: Depends on the project
pay_detail: Not a job. Eligible projects may get funding, not guaranteed.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 13 to 18.
how_to_apply: Wait for the spring 2027 form on the City of Surrey page. Or email the youth team to ask about other ways to join in.
notes: Exact spring 2027 opening day not posted.
duration: A term, meets Thursdays 4:30 to 5:30pm.
pay_detail: Unpaid. You earn volunteer hours.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 13 to 18.
how_to_apply: Drop in. Sign up as a Squad member to hear about more dates and track hours. Groups over 5 email ahead.
notes: Events may be called off in extreme weather. Parks: Serpentine Heights Park (Sep 25, Oct 23) and Godwin Farm Biodiversity Preserve Park (Nov 14).
duration: Drop-in events (length not stated on the program page)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Sign up to track volunteer hours.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18 with permission from a parent or guardian. Spaces are limited.
how_to_apply: Fill in the Teen Volunteer Leadership form on the Nature Center volunteer page. A new form is posted each summer. Questions: Brianna Charbonnel, (253) 404-3930, brianna.charbonnel@tacomaparks.com.
notes: The Nature Center's Youth Council for ages 13 to 18 is on pause. The page also links a Teen Volunteer social story that explains what the week is like.
duration: A two-day training plus one week of summer day camp
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer. Some students can get extra credit or use it for a school project.

who_can_apply: Lifeguard class: be 15 by the last day, pass a swim test on day one, do the online parts first and come to every class. Swim teacher class: be 15 or older, swim 25 yards, tread water for 1 minute, like kids and want to work for Parks Tacoma.
how_to_apply: Register for a lifeguard course through the Register button on the page. Practice the swim test first at a Parks Tacoma pool (free with a Center Pass for ages 18 and under). Then look for openings on GovernmentJobs.com. Questions: aquatics@parkstacoma.gov, (253) 305-1000.
notes: Passing does not guarantee a job. The Red Cross certificate lasts two years and covers pools only. If you get hired, ask whether Washington's minor work papers apply.
duration: Lifeguard course: about 3 days in person plus online modules (for example Nov 20 to 22 or Dec 28 to 30, 2026)
pay_detail: Lifeguard course: $250 for City of Tacoma residents, $275 for others, not refundable. Tacoma residents can ask for financial aid. The swim instructor page gives no fee. Job pay is not stated.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 19. No application. Just come to a meeting at a participating branch or join the Virtual Teen Council.
how_to_apply: Come to a meeting at a Pierce County Library branch that takes part. The page lists the places. You can also join the online council.
notes: Meeting places can change during the year (the page lists 2026-2027 locations and says they are subject to change). Meeting dates are on the library calendar.
duration: October to April, flexible drop-in meetings
pay_detail: Unpaid. Earns volunteer hours.

who_can_apply: Teens (the page does not state an age range). Slots are limited and filled through an application.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the form is posted. Look on the Pierce County Library page about teen volunteering.
notes: The page says teens attend weekly sessions for up to 20 service hours. The page does not state an age range or year. Work permit rule not stated.
duration: 6 weeks, weekly sessions, up to 20 service hours
pay_detail: Unpaid. Up to 20 hours of volunteer service.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 18 and in grades 9 to 12. You should be excited to talk with visitors about nature and animals.
how_to_apply: Apply on the youth volunteer page in December 2026. Large and small group interviews are held in late February; not everyone is interviewed. Join the waitlist form to get an email when applications open.
notes: Most zoo volunteer roles ask for at least one year. Explore the Shore (ages 16 and up) and Spot the Swallows (14 and up with a parent if under 18) are other teen options on the volunteer page. Questions: volunteer@pdza.org or 253-404-3687.
duration: 9 required trainings March to June, then one 6-hour shift a week for 10 weeks in summer
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer.

who_can_apply: Tacoma Public Schools high school students, using their school account. Most experiences start at age 14; some have extra age or schedule rules. Limit of 3 experiences per student.
how_to_apply: Sign in to SchooLinks with your TPS student account. Apply to an experience. Interview with the employer. Then hand in the paperwork and a certificate from a money skills course.
notes: Only for Tacoma Public Schools students. Students new to Jobs 253 get priority. The page caps stipend funds at $1,500 per student and says students must complete a W-9 before starting. Payments typically arrive 4 to 6 weeks after the experience ends. Work permit rule not stated.
duration: Five sessions a year; each internship starts and ends in one session
pay_detail: Up to $500 completion stipend (funded by the City of Tacoma) plus 0.5 elective credit.

who_can_apply: Tacoma Public Schools high school students and students of partner Maritime|253 districts. For the drone course you must be 16 or older to earn the FAA Part 107 certificate. The ANEW program is for ages 16 to 18 with a disability. See its own card.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Tacoma Public Schools Jobs 253 pages when courses are posted. Contact the course lead listed on the page.
notes: Open to TPS and partner district students only. Each course has its own dates, spots and lead; the auto course ran June 22 to July 9 in 2026. Work permit rule not stated.
duration: Varies by course (the auto course ran June 22 to July 9, Monday to Thursday, 8 am to 3 pm)
pay_detail: Free training. $500 stipend at completion.

who_can_apply: You must be at least 15 years old in the calendar year you apply and give one shift a week for at least 3 months.
how_to_apply: Join the email list on the volunteer page (it asks you to confirm you are 15 this year or older). Apply when spring recruitment opens. Questions: volunteer@vanaqua.org.
notes: The aquarium also has a Marine Mammal Rescue Centre volunteer role and practicums. Those are for ages 18 and up, so they are not on this card.
duration: One shift a week for at least 3 months
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer.

who_can_apply: Teens aged 13 to 15. Applicants send a portfolio of 10 images in all. It has 5 to 7 finished works and 3 to 5 sketchbook images. They also send a letter of intent of 500 to 1,000 words.
how_to_apply: Use the APPLY NOW link on the page to submit the portfolio and letter of intent. Questions: submissions@artsumbrella.com or 604-681-5268.
notes: Scholarship-funded learning program, not a paid job. Canada, so British Columbia Employment Standards rules have not been added to this guide yet.
duration: October 2026 to June 2027
pay_detail: Free to students (full scholarship). Not a paid job.

who_can_apply: Students aged 15 to 18, or entering Grades 10, 11 or 12 in fall 2026.
how_to_apply: Apply on the Emily Carr University Continuing Studies site (use the Apply Now link on the page). Questions: teens@ecuad.ca.
notes: Paid-for arts program, not a job. Canada, so British Columbia Employment Standards rules have not been added to this guide yet.
duration: Thursdays 4 to 7 PM, October 15, 2026 to February 11, 2027
pay_detail: Registration fee $555.90 (the page does not state the currency; likely Canadian dollars). Four full-tuition scholarships are available for Indigenous students or students facing financial barriers.

who_can_apply: You must be 16 or older before you apply or go to an information session. Patient contact roles need age 18 or older. Child patient support roles need work or volunteer experience with children.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. Staff will call you for an interview. If you get in, you do a record check, a reference check and training.
notes: The biggest need is Monday to Friday, 8 am to 4 pm; evening and weekend spots usually go to current volunteers. Intake can take several months. If you are not placed within 6 months, the application is closed and you may apply again. Contact: volunteer@cw.bc.ca.
duration: One year for every volunteer role
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer.

who_can_apply: Grade 12 students in BC and the Yukon. From Fall 2026, Grade 11 students are not eligible even if they take Grade 12 level courses. Students in grades 8 to 11 can use the Self-Directed program instead, which offers recorded sessions.
how_to_apply: Register online. You give your contact details and a sponsor teacher's name and email. You give a signed Participant Agreement Form. You give three answers of 150 words or less. After the deadline, students are picked by random draw. Priority goes to First Nations, Inuit and Metis students and to students from different schools.
notes: Registration for the 2026 round is closed. Watch the page for the next round. In person sessions are at 950 West 28th Avenue, Vancouver. This is in Canada, so British Columbia rules apply and this guide has not checked them.
duration: 4 Thursday evenings, 6:30 to 8:00 p.m.
pay_detail: No cost is listed on the page. Attending all sessions makes you eligible to apply for a scholarship with $1,000 CAD toward post-secondary tuition.

who_can_apply: Grade 11 and 12 students in BC and the Yukon. No research experience needed. Limited to the first 1,000 students who apply.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. It asks for your name, contact details, grade and school. It asks for a parent or guardian's contact. It asks for one answer of 150 words or less. Say why you want to attend.
notes: Online talks only, not a job or hands-on lab work. This is in Canada, so British Columbia rules apply and this guide has not checked them. The institute says it does not offer any formal placements for students who want to volunteer, job shadow or gain work experience. The application form link is on the page.
duration: 10 monthly online sessions, Sept 2026 to June 2027, about 1 hour each
pay_detail: Free. You get a certificate of participation if you apply and attend 7 of the 10 sessions.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 30 who need to find work. The page does not list other eligibility rules.
how_to_apply: Click an event under Upcoming Events on the page to apply. Central office: 604-879-6554 or info@bgcbc.ca. Seats are limited.
notes: Canada, so British Columbia Employment Standards rules have not been added to this guide yet. The page did not say where the workshops are held.
duration: 8 weeks per session
pay_detail: Participants are paid to take part, with a completion bonus for finishing all 8 weeks. Amounts are not stated on the page. Free to join.

who_can_apply: High school students in BC, grades 10 to 12 on the research institute page. A teacher must first register the school with the Canadian Medical Hall of Fame. The organizers encourage schools to consider students who are Indigenous, Black, a person of colour, or from rural or lower income backgrounds.
how_to_apply: Ask a teacher to register your school on the Canadian Medical Hall of Fame website (cdnmedhall.ca/discoverydays). The teacher then gets the student sign-up steps. If you cannot find a teacher, email cmhf@cdnmedhall.ca. Give your city, high school and the event.
notes: One day event, not a job. The Medical Hall of Fame page does not name the city, but the research institute page says the event is at 950 West 28th Avenue, Vancouver. This is in Canada, so British Columbia rules apply and this guide has not checked them. Grades come from the institute page only.
pay_detail: No registration fee. You or your school pay for transportation and any parking.

who_can_apply: Age 16 or older for long-term care sites; 18 or older for acute care (hospitals). You must complete a free criminal record check and get a free yearly flu shot or wear a mask.
how_to_apply: Pick a site on the volunteer page (for example Holy Family Hospital, Mount Saint Joseph long-term care or a St. Vincent's site) and fill out its online form. List references like teachers or coaches. If chosen, you will be called for an interview.
notes: At 16 or 17 you can only volunteer at the long-term care sites. There is no shadowing or direct patient care. Most shifts are weekdays during work or school hours. The FAQ also says Public Health requires two COVID-19 shots for volunteers.
duration: 1 to 3 hours a week for at least 4 or 6 months in a row, depending on the program
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer. Volunteers can ask for a reference after 30 hours at long-term care sites.

who_can_apply: Anyone 13 to 18 years old who lives or goes to school in Vancouver.
how_to_apply: Use the 'Click here to apply to ink TAG' form on the ink page. Questions: teens@vpl.ca or 604.331.3690.
notes: You can also send your own writing or art to ink (up to two pieces a year) without joining the group. The page says art or writing made with AI will not be published.
duration: February to December. Meetings every other Thursday during the school year (online or at Central Library), plus two-day summer workshops with mentors.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer.

who_can_apply: Teens 13 to 18 who live in Vancouver. You need a signature from a coach, teacher, counsellor or community leader on your form, and you must come to every session.
how_to_apply: When new sessions are posted, fill in the online form at least one week before the start date. Get your reference person to sign it. Questions: teens@vpl.ca.
notes: If you quit without a good reason, your spot goes to a teen on the waitlist. Sessions are loud and snacks are provided.
duration: One hour a week for about 8 weeks, plus a teen training session on the first date. Arrive 15 minutes early.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer. You earn community service hours, and the library can write a letter confirming them.

who_can_apply: Teens 13 to 18 who live in Vancouver. You must come to every session.
how_to_apply: When new sessions are posted, fill in the online form on the STEAM Buddies page at least one week before the start date. Questions: teens@vpl.ca.
notes: Like Reading Buddies, but with hands-on science and tech. Check the page each season for new branches and dates.
duration: One hour a week for about 4 weeks, plus a teen training session on the first date.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer. You earn community service hours.

who_can_apply: Anyone 13 to 18 years old who lives in Vancouver.
how_to_apply: Fill in the online application form linked on the TAG page. Pick the online group or a branch group (Central Library, Kensington, Kerrisdale, Kitsilano or Renfrew). Questions: teens@vpl.ca.
notes: Some branch groups fill up, so the online Teams group may be the easiest to join. Event listings on the library calendar show exact dates and access details.
duration: September to June. One hour every other week (4 to 5 p.m.), online on Teams or at a branch.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer. Members earn community service hours.

who_can_apply: Teens 13 to 18 who know some D&D. Teens who live or go to school in Vancouver get first pick. You need an adult reference who is not your parent or guardian.
how_to_apply: Fill in the application form on the Teen DMs page and give the contact for an adult reference (a coach, teacher, counsellor or community leader). Questions: teens@vpl.ca.
notes: Some times of year are busier than others, so you may wait a while for your first game.
duration: Varies. Times and branches change, and some are one-time events.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer. You earn community service hours.

who_can_apply: Teens who live in Vancouver. The page does not give an age range.
how_to_apply: Watch the teensatvpl Instagram for featured books. Ask for one by Instagram message or at teens@vpl.ca. Pick it up at your nearest branch, then email your rating and review to teens@vpl.ca.
notes: Share your opinion of the book, not a summary of the plot. Reviews of only one or two lines are sent back for more detail.
duration: At your own pace, one book at a time
pay_detail: Unpaid. You get one community service hour for every 100 pages of the book, confirmed by letter.

who_can_apply: Core volunteer program: at least 16 years old, 100 hours minimum. High School Work Experience: Lower Mainland students in Grades 11 and 12; teachers sign students up.
how_to_apply: Check the volunteer page for the next intake. For the work experience placement, ask your teacher to sign you up.
notes: The Science World Teen Advisory Group (ages 16 to 18) is on hiatus and not taking applications (page checked 2026-10-09). Volunteer role in Canada; British Columbia Employment Standards rules have not been added to this guide yet.
duration: 100 hours minimum, one 2 to 3 hour shift per week
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer.

who_can_apply: Indigenous (First Nations, Metis or Inuit) high school students in grades 9 to 12. You live in Metro Vancouver or Kelowna.
how_to_apply: Watch the seed2STEM page for the application. Email seed2STEM@icord.org or call 604-675-8830.
notes: Exact opening day not posted.
duration: 6 weeks
pay_detail: Minimum wage for 25 hours a week. Transit passes, loaner laptops, some meals and youth support workers are provided.

who_can_apply: Must be 14 years of age by June 29, 2026. If accepted, you submit a criminal record check and complete training.
how_to_apply: Submit the online volunteer application, attend one in-person interview, then complete in-person or online training. Returning volunteers can apply as Lead Volunteers by email.
notes: SFU Camps says it is not a registered non-profit; check with your teacher that your school accepts these hours for service or work experience credit. Top volunteers are encouraged to apply as paid instructors later (2026 instructor wage $27.05 to $28.50 per hour, CAD); the minimum age for instructors is not stated on the page. Volunteer role in Canada; British Columbia Employment Standards rules have not been added to this guide yet.
duration: Minimum 2 weeks (at least 80 hours), consecutive or separate
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteers get volunteer hours, evaluations, confirmation letters and a reference request option.

who_can_apply: Teens age 16 and older, and adults. No other rule is stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Fill out the "Volunteer with us" form linked on the Space Centre careers page. Questions can go to careers@spacecentre.ca.
notes: Age 16 and up, so 13 to 15 year olds cannot apply. The pages do not give shift length, hours or a start date, so ask before you plan.
