This is in Canada, so British Columbia rules apply and this guide has not checked them. Rechecked 2026-10-10: the volunteer page loads and confirms age 16 and up, the summer Augmented Reality role and the "Volunteer with us" form. It gives no year, dates or deadline.
duration: Not stated. The summer Augmented Reality role is weekly support.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role. The page lists education and skills training and mentions telescope viewing on some evening shifts as a volunteer benefit.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 17 can join EcoStewards, DIRT, Nature House Hosts, EcoRangers and EcoCamp Assistants. Ages 12 to 15 can join only EcoStewards, and only with adult supervision. A parent or guardian must sign the youth consent form.
how_to_apply: Register and sign up through Better Impact. If a role is closed, fill in the Volunteer Interest Form. Email vols@stanleyparkecology.ca with questions.
notes: Volunteer role in Canada. British Columbia Employment Standards rules have not been added to this guide yet, so work permit is marked unknown. Most other roles on the site are for volunteers 16 and older.
duration: Varies by role; many are seasonal
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer. Volunteers can request a reference letter after 25 hours.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 15 to 18 who have completed grade 10 or equivalent. UBC recommends about a 78% average, 3.5 GPA, B average or IB 5. Students still learning English should have IELTS 6.0 or TOEFL 80 or higher. Open to students from other countries.
how_to_apply: No application, transcripts or proof of English are needed. Check that you are eligible. Add a course or mini school to your cart. Have a parent or guardian create a Family Account. Pay the deposit at checkout. Then finish the information package within 48 hours.
notes: Costs money, and it is a camp-style university course, not a job. This is in Canada, so British Columbia rules apply and this guide has not checked them. The fee table is labeled 2026 and still shows a 'due May 1, 2026' date next to the 2027 sessions, so check the 2027 fees before you plan. An online version also exists (3 week courses); this card covers the on-campus version. Rechecked 2026-10-10: the on-campus page confirms the 2027 session dates and the residence and commuter deadlines on this card. It does not say when 2027 registration opens. It still labels the fee table 2026.
duration: 2 weeks per session
pay_detail: 2026 fees listed in CAD: course $1,940 for Canadian students (including permanent residents) or $2,620 international; mini school $2,110 Canadian or $2,855 international. Optional residence add-on $2,650. A $500 deposit is due when you register. Fees can change. The President Bursary is for B.C. grade 11 students with financial need.

who_can_apply: First Nations, Inuit or Metis students going into grades 9 to 12. Week 1 is for students going into grades 11 or 12. Week 2 is for students going into grades 9 or 10. The pages do not state an age rule.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Summer Science application online (UBC form). Or send it by email to summer.science@ubc.ca, or by mail. A reference letter of about 200 words is recommended. It can come from a teacher, coach, mentor or community leader.
notes: Only for Indigenous students (First Nations, Inuit, Metis). It is a camp, not a job. This is in Canada, so British Columbia rules apply and this guide has not checked them. The page still shows 2025 dates, so check the newest page before you plan. The application page lists the 2026 deadline of June 15, 2026.
duration: 1 week
pay_detail: $200 program fee covers housing and meals. Workshops and Vancouver Aquarium admission are covered. Bursaries for students with financial need and travel bursaries are available. Travel to Vancouver is not included.

who_can_apply: Teens going into Grade 10, 11 or 12 who live or go to school in Vancouver. You must want to finish school and not miss a lot of it. You cannot have serious arrests, a record of trouble with police, or gang ties.
how_to_apply: Apply online with the Apply Now button on the VPD Cadet page when it reopens in spring 2027. Questions: cadets@vpd.ca.
notes: About 90 cadets a year. It is a leadership program, not police recruiting. The VPD Indigenous Cadet Program is a different summer job for ages 19 to 29. Unpaid, so BC child employment rules for paid work do not apply here.
duration: 28 weeks, September to May
pay_detail: Free. The Vancouver Police Foundation pays for all program materials and fees.

who_can_apply: Vancouver School Board students. Apply in grade 11 for grade 12, semester 2, at John Oliver Secondary. Grade 12 students can apply if a space is left.
how_to_apply: Use the application on the page or ask your counsellor. Email careerprograms@vsb.bc.ca.
notes: Page says students should apply in grade 11, and that grade 12 students can apply if a space remains. Confirm with the school. Contact Mark Reid, Career Programs Teacher, mreid@vsb.bc.ca.
duration: Semester 2 of grade 12
pay_detail: Not stated

who_can_apply: Students in grades 10 to 12 at Vancouver School Board schools. You need an employer in a known trade. The employer, you, a parent and the district sign an agreement.
how_to_apply: Email careerprograms@vsb.bc.ca. For building trades, ask to join the SiteReady safety course.
notes: Contact Mark Reid at the program. Students who need only one or two classes can work four days a week and take self-paced classes at South Hill Education Centre.
duration: Credits earned over the school year or semester
pay_detail: Paid by the employer. Rate not stated.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 18 as of Dec 31, in the Vancouver region. This includes Vancouver, North Vancouver, West Vancouver, Burnaby and Richmond. A youth group, like a school or community group, must name you. Five members of that group must sign.
how_to_apply: Download the form. Find a sponsor group and five people to name you. Add a personal note if you did not take part last year. Fill out the online form and upload your files.
notes: Contact vyp@bcyp.org for session questions and registrar@bcyp.org for applying. The 40th session dates were not posted when read.
duration: One weekend session plus events during the year
pay_detail: $60 registration fee; financial help may be asked for by email

who_can_apply: High school students in partner school districts, including Vancouver, Surrey, Richmond and Langley. Process starts in grade 11 for courses in grade 12.
how_to_apply: Talk to the career staff at your school district. You need two references, a letter from a counselor or school leader, a letter from a parent, and the form.
notes: Recommended B or higher in English 11 and Math 11. Tuition amounts are from the VCC page and can change. Ask your district whether it pays.
duration: Varies by program (about 6 months to 40 weeks)
pay_detail: VCC lists program tuition (for example $2,513 for Baking Foundation High School). Application and student fees are waived if accepted. School district may pay tuition for select courses.

who_can_apply: Youth starting at age 5 up to those who have not yet reached their 19th birthday on October 1 of the current 4-H year. Clubs run through your county WSU Extension office.
how_to_apply: Choose your project or projects. Find a club through your county WSU Extension 4-H office. Or start one if none exists. Talk with local staff, then enroll through 4-H Online. Then go to meetings and events.
notes: Fees, clubs and projects differ by county. This is a youth club and leadership program, not a paid job.
duration: One 4-H year. Enrollment opens each Oct. 1.
pay_detail: The statewide Join page does not list fees. Fees may be set by county, so ask your local Extension office.

who_can_apply: Washington state residents who are high school juniors (per the 2025 WAS FAQ: 'Scholars must be a Washington state resident and be a current junior in high school'). No math or science prerequisites are listed on the page.
how_to_apply: Fill out the WAS 2026-27 Program Application linked on the page. Questions: WAS@museumofflight.org or 206-768-7214. Phase 2 invitations use a lottery. It is among students who meet the Phase 1 requirements.
notes: Deadline is very close. Graduates can apply for Museum scholarships. Participation in Phase 2 is not required for Phase 1. Students who are not juniors yet can fill out the Program Interest Form on the page to be contacted when they are eligible.
duration: Phase 1: November through March (15-20 hours per two-week lesson). Phase 2: six-day residency in July or August.
pay_detail: Phase 1 online course is free (optional 5 UW credits cost $255; financial assistance up to 100% available). Optional Phase 2 six-day residency costs $1,850 including room and board; tuition assistance up to 100% available.

who_can_apply: Students in a business or marketing class taught by a CTE certified teacher at a school with a DECA chapter. The official page lists no age or grade rule.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's DECA advisor, who registers members through DECA's online system. If your school has no chapter, DECA lists six steps to start one. State advisor: Lori Hairston, lori@wadeca.org.
notes: DECA's page lists 187 chapters in Washington. The state site is wadeca.org.
duration: School year
pay_detail: Student membership is $20 total: $12 to the state association and $8 to DECA Inc. Chapters may add local costs.

who_can_apply: Any high school junior, typically a 16 or 17 year old finishing 11th grade. No political experience is needed. The program is for both boys and girls.
how_to_apply: Apply yourself with the online application at ebgs-wa.org/apply. Or ask a teacher, counselor or local American Legion Post to nominate you. They use the program's nomination form. After screening, the program helps find a sponsor if you need one.
notes: The site describes a 7-day, 6-night leadership experience. Confirm the 2027 dates on the main page of ebgs-wa.org.
duration: One week. 2027 session: Sunday June 20 to Saturday June 26, 2027.
pay_detail: The program is valued at $700 with meals and housing. A local American Legion Post can sponsor a student for $350 on request, and help for the full $700 is available on request. The site says cost is not a barrier.

who_can_apply: Students enrolled in agricultural education at a school with an FFA chapter. The page does not give age or grade limits.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's ag teacher if your school has an FFA chapter and how to join.
notes: The page says the association has over 14,500 members in 194 chapters. Dues are $7 a year nationally and $10 a year for Washington. Local chapters may charge more.
duration: Ongoing
pay_detail: Not stated on the program pages. Ask your ag teacher about dues.

who_can_apply: Teens. The page does not state an age or grade rule. Teen volunteering is available at the Bainbridge Island, Bremerton (Sylvan Way), Port Orchard, Poulsbo and Silverdale branches.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Volunteer Application online. It shows which branches have openings.
notes: The application form did not load for this guide, so the questions and age rule were not checked. Call your branch to confirm the minimum age.
duration: Not stated

who_can_apply: At least 14 years old and not yet 17. You need a parent or guardian's permission and a teacher's recommendation.
how_to_apply: Apply online when applications open on the Page Program page. Pick the weeks you can do with care. Senate contact: SenatePageProgram@leg.wa.gov, 360-786-7498. House contact: 360-786-7889.
notes: The page lists no closing date, so apply soon after Nov 1. Check the Page Program page for the current application link. Paid work for people under 18 in Washington needs a parent and school authorization form (the employer holds the Minor Work Permit). See permit.html?state=wa for the exact permit and steps.
duration: One week during the session. The 2027 session runs January through April.
pay_detail: Stipend of $67 per day. You need a Social Security card to get it. Pages without one can still take part but get no daily stipend.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 15 to 18. The page describes it as for urban teens. Crews go home each night for the first four weeks.
how_to_apply: Use the apply link for Tacoma or Olympia on the page. Ask about tuition help.
notes: Teens may be able to get school credit, but only your school can decide. Participants who leave early get a prorated stipend and lose bonuses.
duration: 5 weeks (2026: June 22 to July 24 and July 28 to Aug 28)
pay_detail: Stipend of $96 a day (up to $480 a week) plus $20 weekly dependability bonus and $20 weekly safety bonus. $200 tuition, with tuition help based on need.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 15 to 18 who can travel to the central meeting place each day. Housing is not provided.
how_to_apply: Use the Tacoma apply link on the page. Ask about tuition help.
notes: Crews may earn high school credit if your school agrees. The same program also runs in Eugene, OR and Boise, ID.
duration: 5 weeks, Monday to Friday (2026: June 22 to July 24 and July 28 to Aug 28)
pay_detail: Stipend of $96 a day (up to $480 a week) plus $20 weekly dependability bonus and $20 weekly safety bonus. $200 tuition, with tuition help based on need.

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors in Washington. The SBCTC page does not list other requirements; contact the college's Running Start coordinator.
how_to_apply: Contact the Running Start coordinator at the college you want to attend (the SBCTC page links a coordinator list) and your high school counselor.
notes: Work hours tie-in from Washington L&I: 16 and 17 year olds enrolled in a bona fide college program, such as Running Start, may work non-school week hours during the regular school year (employers should ask for proof such as a college transcript).
duration: Per quarter or semester
pay_detail: No tuition. Students and families pay mandatory fees, books and transportation.

who_can_apply: Volunteers of all ages. Volunteers 13 and under must be supervised by a parent or guardian.
how_to_apply: Contact the volunteer coordinator at your local library for a list of openings, or use the Volunteer Portal on the page.
notes: Library jobs at Sno-Isle require you to be 16 or older (from the same page). The page says to check with your local library for current openings.
duration: A regular portion of your time each week

who_can_apply: Ages 12 through 18 (national Civil Air Patrol page). The Washington Wing pages do not list other rules. Ask a squadron about citizenship and school rules.
how_to_apply: Find a squadron on the Washington Wing Locations list or the national unit finder. Visit a meeting. Ask the squadron for the application. Wing office: 253-982-7774 or wa@wawg.cap.gov.
notes: The Washington Wing join page links to separate Youth, Adults and Educators pages, so the age and cost figures come from the national page. This is a youth program, not a paid job.
duration: The national page describes about a 2-hour squadron meeting each week, a monthly Saturday event and a week-long summer encampment. School-based squadrons may differ.
pay_detail: National Civil Air Patrol page: annual dues of $25 to $50 depending on location, and about $300 to $600 in costs in the first year, less any financial assistance. Ask your squadron for exact costs.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 10 to 18. Under 14 must have a parent, guardian or teacher with them.
how_to_apply: Search the WTA work party list, pick one and sign up online. Youth groups can contact WTA to set up a private work party.
notes: The overview page does not say whether youth work parties are unpaid; it describes them as volunteer service hours. Multi-day shared-identity trail trips are also offered. Details on gear, rides and sign-up are on the work party page, not read here. Youth group bookings: volunteer@wta.org.
duration: Work parties run Tuesday to Sunday; one day or multi-day
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering

who_can_apply: Washington residents who are U.S. citizens or lawful permanent residents, ages 15 and a half to 18 at entry (the main page says 15 to 18). You must be behind in school, have dropped out, or be at risk of not graduating. No felony charges or pending court cases. You must choose to attend, stay drug free and be able to take part.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Send the doctor and dentist forms and other documents (WYA.Applications@mil.wa.gov or fax 360-473-2623). Then do an interview and final review. Phone: 877-228-8947.
notes: This is for teens who are off track in school, not a job program. Campus: 1207 Carver Street, Bremerton, WA 98312.
duration: 22 weeks on campus (a 147-day class cycle), then a two-year follow-up phase
pay_detail: Free. The page calls it a free life intervention and credit retrieval program.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 30 who have no job or not enough work. You must have the right to work in Canada. You must face barriers to work or more school. The page says barriers are required.
how_to_apply: Register on the page or go to an info session. Email nextstep@ywcabc.org or call 236-985-4551.
notes: The page gives both six and seven weeks of group workshops, so confirm the schedule. The card url redirects to ywcabc.org. Other YWCA youth programs are not listed here.
duration: 12 weeks (7 weeks of workshops, 5 weeks one-to-one)
pay_detail: Free. Financial incentives for finishing milestones and a completion bonus (amounts not stated).
